title: Normalized Kummer target from its unshifted positive boundary comparison
statement: For a prime l, a scheme T with l invertible, Kummer data k and any Reduction r for Rrings l T, there are a module system M, an isomorphism i from its underlying tower to roots l T, and an isomorphism b from r applied to units[1] to M[2], satisfying exactly targetNormalization for the positive boundary of k. No reduction functor or integer-source comparison is constructed.

proof.text: Construct the shift structure on r.derived as the one induced by its adjunction to exact forgetting, using Mathlib Adjunction.leftAdjointCommShift and commShift_of_rightAdjoint. Compose the shift comparison of r.derived with c[1] and the inverse of shiftFunctorAdd(1,1) to define b. The private shift_mate lemma uses the adjunction-unit shift identity and shift naturality to identify its adjunct. The private shift_add_map lemma uses commShiftIso_add to commute forgetting with the shift-addition map. The generic private shift_normalization lemma combines these identities with naturality of shiftFunctorAdd and the unshifted normalization. The private derived_target_normalization adapter carries out the single-functor and targetNormalization conversions over abstract abelian categories. Pass the three short-complex endpoints explicitly when applying that adapter to the derived tower categories, avoiding kernel reduction through the localization construction to compare a short-complex projection and obtaining exactly targetNormalization. Return M, i and b with that target normalization. Store the comparison and its normalization in the private TargetNormalizationData record. The generic normalize_targets helper performs the existential assembly over abstract abelian categories, so the scheme-specific theorem is a direct application and does not unpack the derived comparisons at concrete localization types.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_normalizedKummerTarget (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime]
    (T : Scheme.{u}) (hT : IsUnit (l : Γ(T, ⊤))) (k : Kummer l T)
    (r : Reduction T (Rrings l T)) :
    ∃ (M : Systems T (Rrings l T)) (i : r.forget.F.obj M ≅ roots l T)
      (b : r.derived.obj (((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (Ab T) 0).obj
        (units T))⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧) ≅
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (Systems T (Rrings l T)) 0).obj M)⟦(2 : ℤ)⟧),
      r.model.targetNormalization (ShortComplex.mk k.inclusion k.power k.zero)
        k.exact b i
